branches.name: Foundations of soil science
branches.why: the course opener; holds what soil is and the discipline's own branches

branches.name: Soil composition
branches.why: mineral, organic, water and air phases of soil

branches.name: Parent materials and weathering
branches.why: the geologic starting point of pedogenesis

branches.name: Soil morphology and profile description
branches.why: field description and diagnostic horizons

branches.name: Pedology and soil genesis
branches.why: soil-forming factors and pedogenic processes; IUSS Division 1

branches.name: Soil geography
branches.why: world distribution of soils and soil-landscape sequences is a recognized branch (IUSS Commission 1.1); the frame has no home for it

branches.name: Soil geomorphology and wetland soils
branches.why: soils on landforms, hydric and subaqueous soils

branches.name: Soil classification
branches.why: national and international classification systems; IUSS Commission 1.4

branches.name: USDA Soil Taxonomy
branches.why: the orders and suborders of Soil Taxonomy

branches.name: World Reference Base
branches.why: WRB reference soil groups

branches.name: Other and regional soil types
branches.why: named soil types outside the two main systems

branches.name: Soil mineralogy
branches.why: soil mineralogy is an SSSA division and IUSS commission (2.4); the course treats only clay minerals and has no home for primary minerals, oxides, weathering sequences or identification methods

branches.name: Clay mineralogy and soil colloids
branches.why: layer silicates, oxides and colloid behaviour

branches.name: Soil micromorphology
branches.why: a recognized branch (IUSS Commission 1.2) with its own methods; the course has a single entry for it

branches.name: Soil physics: texture and structure
branches.why: particles, aggregates and structure; SSSA Soil Physics division

branches.name: Soil mechanics and compaction
branches.why: density, pores, strength and compaction where soil science meets geotechnics

branches.name: Soil hydrology and hydropedology
branches.why: soil water retention, flow and the field water balance

branches.name: Solute transport in soil
branches.why: solute and contaminant transport through the vadose zone is a core advanced topic of soil physics with no chapter

branches.name: Soil thermal regime, aeration and frozen ground
branches.why: heat, gas exchange and freezing in soil

branches.name: Soil surface chemistry and ion exchange
branches.why: charge, exchange and humic substances

branches.name: Soil solution chemistry, sorption and speciation
branches.chapter: new: Soil solution chemistry and sorption
branches.why: sorption isotherms, surface complexation, speciation and kinetics are the advanced core of soil chemistry (SSSA Soil Chemistry division); the frame has no chapter for them

branches.name: Soil redox chemistry
branches.why: oxidation-reduction in wet soils

branches.name: Soil acidity, alkalinity and salinity
branches.why: pH, sodicity and salt-affected soils

branches.name: Soil analysis and laboratory methods
branches.chapter: new: Soil analysis and laboratory methods
branches.why: sampling, extraction and instrumental analysis are taught as their own course and SSSA area; methods are scattered or missing

branches.name: Soil biology and ecology
branches.why: soil organisms and food webs; SSSA Soil Biology and Biochemistry division

branches.name: Soil biochemistry and microbial ecology methods
branches.why: enzymes, microbial carbon use, stoichiometry and molecular methods form the biochemistry half of SSSA's Soil Biology and Biochemistry division; the course has only scattered entries

branches.name: Rhizosphere and plant-microbe symbioses
branches.why: roots, mycorrhizae and nodulation

branches.name: Soil organic matter
branches.why: litter, decomposition and humus

branches.name: Soil fertility and plant nutrition
branches.why: SSSA Soil Fertility and Plant Nutrition division

branches.name: Nutrient biogeochemistry
branches.why: N, P, S, K and other element cycles in soil

branches.name: Fertilizers, manures and amendments
branches.why: materials added to soil

branches.name: Soil erosion and sedimentation
branches.why: water, wind and gravity erosion

branches.name: Farming systems, irrigation and growing media
branches.why: cropping systems, irrigation and substrates

branches.name: Tillage and cultivation
branches.why: tillage systems and implements

branches.name: Soil and water conservation
branches.why: conservation practices; IUSS Commission 3.2

branches.name: Soil survey and land evaluation
branches.why: mapping practice and land evaluation; IUSS Commission 1.3 and 4.1

branches.name: Pedometrics and digital soil mapping
branches.chapter: new: Pedometrics and digital soil mapping
branches.why: pedometrics is an IUSS commission (1.5) and SSSA working area; geostatistics, sensing and digital mapping have no home in a 14-entry survey chapter

branches.name: Forest and rangeland soils
branches.why: SSSA has a Forest, Range and Wildland Soils division; the course has only scattered forest entries and nothing on rangeland soils

branches.name: Urban and human-made soils
branches.why: anthropogenic soils are an IUSS working group (SUITMA) and a WRB class; Technosols, constructed soils and urban soils are scattered or missing

branches.name: Soil carbon and climate
branches.why: soil carbon cycling and greenhouse gases

branches.name: Land degradation and desertification
branches.why: soil and land degradation

branches.name: Soil health, policy and protection
branches.why: soil health, governance and protection

branches.name: Soil contamination and remediation
branches.why: pollutants and remediation; SSSA environmental quality division

branches.name: Soils and human health
branches.why: soils and human health (medical geology, soil-borne disease, geophagy, micronutrient deficiency) is an IUSS working area and recent textbook chapter; the course has nothing on it

branches.name: Paleopedology and soil dating
branches.why: paleopedology is an IUSS commission (1.6); paleosol entries are spread over four chapters and soil dating methods are missing

branches.name: Forensic and archaeological soil science
branches.chapter: new: Forensic and archaeological soil science
branches.why: geoarchaeology and forensic soil science are recognized applied branches (IUSS working group on soils and archaeology); the course has only incidental entries

branches.name: History of soil science
branches.why: IUSS Commission 4.5

branches.name: Founders and pioneers
branches.why: the field's founders

branches.name: Societies and journals
branches.why: the field's institutions and literature

branches.name: Astropedology
branches.why: regolith and soils of other worlds
